lines: Habits are a funny thing. We reach for them **mindlessly**, setting our brains on auto-pilot and relaxing into the unconscious comfort of familiar routine. “Not choice, but habit rules the unreflecting herd,” William Wordsworth said in the 19th century. In the ever-changing 21st century, even the word “habit” carries a negative implication. So it seems paradoxical to talk about habits in the same context as creativity and innovation. But brain researchers have discovered that when we consciously develop new habits, we create **parallel** paths, and even entirely new brain cells, that can jump our trains of thought onto new, innovative tracks.

习惯是个有趣的东西。我们不经思索地依赖习惯，让大脑进入自动导航状态，在熟悉惯例带来的无意识的安逸中放松下来。19世纪，威廉·华兹华斯说过：“驾驭不加思索的芸芸众生的，不是选择，而是习惯。”在瞬息万变的21世纪，就连“习惯”一词也带上了贬义。因此，把习惯与创造、创新放在同一语境下谈论，似乎自相矛盾。但大脑研究人员发现，当我们有意识地培养新习惯时，我们会开辟出平行的神经通路，甚至创造出全新的脑细胞，使我们的思维跃上新的、具有创新性的轨道。

lines: Rather than dismissing ourselves as unchangeable creatures of habit, we can instead **direct** our own change by consciously developing new habits. lines: “The first thing needed for innovation is a **fascination** with wonder,” says Dawna Markova, author of The Open Mind. “But we are taught instead to 'decide,' just as our president calls himself 'the Decider.'” She adds, however, that “to decide is to kill off all possibilities but one. A good innovational thinker is always exploring the many other possibilities.”

lines: All of us work through problems in ways of which we're unaware, she says. Researchers in the late 1960s discovered that humans are born with the capacity to approach challenges in four primary ways: analytically, procedurally, relationally (or collaboratively) and **innovatively**. At the end of adolescence, however, the brain shuts down half of that capacity, preserving only those modes of thought that have seemed most valuable during the first decade or so of life.
她说，我们所有人解决问题的方式，连自己都意识不到。20世纪60年代末的研究人员发现，人类天生具备四种应对挑战的基本方式：分析型、程序型、关联型（或协作型）和创新型。然而，青春期结束时，大脑会关闭其中一半的能力，只保留在人生头十年左右显得最有价值的那些思维模式。

lines: The current emphasis on standardized testing highlights analysis and **procedure**, meaning that few of us inherently use our innovative and collaborative modes of thought. “This breaks the major rule in the American belief system — that anyone can do anything,” explains M. J. Ryan, author of the 2006 book This Year I Will... and Ms. Markova's business partner. “That's a lie that we have perpetuated, and it fosters **commonness**. Knowing what you're good at and doing even more of it creates excellence.” This is where developing new habits comes in.
当前对标准化测试的强调突出了分析和程序，这意味着我们当中很少有人会去运用固有的创新型和协作型思维模式。“这违背了美国信念体系中的首要准则——人人皆能无所不为，”2006年出版的《今年我决心……》一书的作者、马尔科娃女士的生意伙伴M. J. 瑞安解释道。“这是我们长期延续的一个谎言，它助长了平庸。知道自己擅长什么，并做得更多，才能造就卓越。”这正是培养新习惯的意义所在。

lines: But some observers are skeptical. “There's a kind of false precision being hawked by people claiming they are doing ancestry testing,” says Troy Duster, a New York University sociologist. He notes that each individual has many ancestors — numbering in the hundreds just a few centuries back. Yet most ancestry testing only considers a single **lineage**, either the Y chromosome inherited through men in a father's line or mitochondrial DNA, which is passed down only from mothers. This DNA can reveal genetic information about only one or two ancestors, even though, for example, just three generations back people also have six other great-grandparents or, four generations back, 14 other great-great-grandparents.
但一些观察家对此持怀疑态度。“那些声称在做血统检测的人兜售的是一种虚假的精确，”纽约大学社会学家特洛伊·达斯特说。他指出，每个人的祖先众多——仅仅几代人之前就数以百计。然而大多数血统检测只考虑单一的谱系：要么是通过父系男性遗传的Y染色体，要么是只由母亲传递的线粒体DNA。这种DNA只能揭示一两位祖先的遗传信息，而实际上，往上数三代，一个人还有六位曾外祖父母，往上数四代，还有14位高祖父母。

lines: Critics also argue that commercial genetic testing is only as good as the **reference** collections to which a sample is compared. Databases used by some companies don't rely on data collected systematically but rather lump together information from different research projects. This means that a DNA database may have a lot of data from some regions and not others, so a person's test results may differ depending on the company that processes the results. In addition, the computer programs a company uses to estimate relationships may be patented and not subject to peer review or outside evaluation.

lines: The relationship between formal education and economic growth in poor countries is widely misunderstood by economists and politicians alike. Progress in both areas is undoubtedly necessary for the social, political, and intellectual development of these and all other societies; however, the conventional view that education should be one of the very highest **priorities** for promoting rapid economic development in poor countries is wrong. We are fortunate that it is, because building new educational systems there and putting enough people through them to improve economic performance would require two or three generations. The findings of a research institution have consistently shown that workers in all countries can be trained on the job to achieve **radically** higher productivity and, as a result, radically higher standards of living.

穷国的正规教育与经济增长之间的关系，被经济学家和政治家们普遍误解了。这两个领域的进步对穷国乃至所有其他国家的社会、政治和智力发展无疑都是必要的；然而，那种认为教育应当成为推动穷国经济快速发展之最高优先事项之一的传统看法是错误的。所幸这种看法是错误的，因为在这些国家建立新的教育体制、让足够多的人接受这种教育以改善经济表现，需要两三代人的时间。一家研究机构的研究结果一贯表明，所有国家的工人都可以通过在职培训来实现生产率的大幅提高，从而实现生活水平的大幅提高。

lines: As education improved, humanity's productivity potential increased as well. When the competitive environment pushed our ancestors to achieve that potential, they could in turn afford more education. This increasingly high level of education is probably a necessary, but not a sufficient, condition for the complex political systems required by advanced economic performance. Thus poor countries might not be able to escape their poverty traps without political changes that may be possible only with broader formal education. A lack of formal education, however, doesn't constrain the ability of the developing world's workforce to substantially improve productivity for the foreseeable future. On the contrary, constraints on improving productivity explain why education isn't developing more quickly there than it is.

随着教育的改善，人类的生产率潜力也随之提高。当竞争环境促使我们的祖先发挥这种潜力时，他们反过来又有能力接受更多的教育。这种越来越高的教育水平，对于先进经济表现所需要的复杂政治体制而言，可能是必要但非充分的条件。因此，穷国若不进行政治变革也许无法摆脱贫困陷阱，而政治变革只有在更普及的正规教育之下才有可能实现。然而，缺乏正规教育并不会限制发展中国家劳动力在可预见的未来大幅提高生产率的能力。恰恰相反，生产率提高所受到的制约，才解释了为什么那里的教育发展没有比现在更快。

lines: The most thoroughly studied intellectuals in the history of the New World are the ministers and political leaders of seventeenth-century New England. According to the standard history of American philosophy, nowhere else in colonial America was “so much importance attached to intellectual **pursuits**.” According to many books and articles, New England's leaders established the basic themes and preoccupations of an unfolding, dominant Puritan tradition in American intellectual life.
在美洲新大陆历史上，被研究得最透彻的知识分子是17世纪新英格兰的牧师和政治领袖。按照美国哲学史的标准叙述，在殖民地时代的美洲，没有其他地方“如此重视对知识的追求”。许多书刊认为，新英格兰的领袖们确立了正在形成的、占主导地位的清教传统在美国精神生活中的基本主题和关注点。

lines: To take this approach to the New Englanders normally means to start with the Puritans' theological innovations and their distinctive ideas about the church — important subjects that we may not neglect. But in keeping with our examination of southern intellectual life, we may consider the original Puritans as **carriers** of European culture, adjusting to New World circumstances. The New England colonies were the scenes of important episodes in the pursuit of widely understood ideals of civility and virtuosity.
以这种思路研究新英格兰人，通常意味着从清教徒的神学创新和他们关于教会的独特观念入手——这些都是不可忽视的重要课题。但为了与我们对南部精神生活的考察保持一致，我们可以把最初的清教徒视为欧洲文化的携带者，他们正在适应新大陆的环境。新英格兰殖民地是追求公认的文明与修养理想的重要舞台。

lines: The early settlers of Massachusetts Bay included men of impressive education and influence in England. Besides the ninety or so learned ministers who came to Massachusetts churches in the decade after 1629, there were political leaders like John Winthrop, an educated gentleman, lawyer, and official of the Crown before he journeyed to Boston. lines: We should not forget, however, that most New Englanders were less well educated. While few craftsmen or farmers, let alone dependents and servants, left literary compositions to be analyzed, it is obvious that their views were less fully **intellectualized**. Their thinking often had a traditional superstitious quality. A tailor named John Dane, who emigrated in the late 1630s, left an account of his reasons for leaving England that is filled with signs. Sexual confusion, economic frustrations, and religious hope — all came together in a decisive moment when he opened the Bible, told his father that the first line he saw would settle his fate, and read the magical words: “Come out from among them, touch no unclean thing, and I will be your God and you shall be my people.” One wonders what Dane thought of the careful sermons explaining the Bible that he heard in Puritan churches.

然而我们不应忘记，大多数新英格兰人的教育程度较低。由于几乎没有什么工匠或农夫——更不用说侍从和仆人——留下可供分析的文字作品，显而易见，他们的思想没有那么充分的知识化。他们的思维常常带有传统的迷信色彩。一位名叫约翰·戴恩的裁缝于17世纪30年代末移民，他留下了关于自己离开英格兰缘由的记述，其中充满了各种预兆。性的困惑、经济上的挫折和宗教上的希望——所有这些在决定性的时刻交汇：他翻开《圣经》，告诉父亲他看到的第一行字将决定他的命运，然后读到了那句神启之言：“从他们中间出来吧，不要碰不洁之物，我必作你们的神，你们必作我的子民。”人们不禁想知道，戴恩对他在清教教堂里听到的那些严谨解经的布道会作何感想。

lines: Coinciding with the groundbreaking theory of biological evolution proposed by British naturalist Charles Darwin in the 1860s, British social philosopher Herbert Spencer put forward his own theory of biological and cultural evolution. Spencer argued that all worldly phenomena, including human societies, changed over time, advancing toward perfection. (41) ______.
19世纪60年代，正当英国博物学家查尔斯·达尔文提出开创性的生物进化论之时，英国社会哲学家赫伯特·斯宾塞提出了自己的生物与文化进化理论。斯宾塞认为，包括人类社会在内的一切世间现象都随时间推移而变化，并不断走向完善。(41)______。

lines: American social scientist Lewis Henry Morgan introduced another theory of cultural evolution in the late 1800s. Morgan helped found modern anthropology — the scientific study of human societies, customs and beliefs — thus becoming one of the earliest anthropologists. In his work, he attempted to show how all aspects of culture changed together in the evolution of societies. (42) ______.
19世纪末，美国社会科学家路易斯·亨利·摩尔根提出了另一种文化进化理论。摩尔根参与创建了现代人类学——对人类社会、风俗和信仰的科学研究——从而成为最早的人类学家之一。在他的著作中，他试图展示在社会的演化进程中，文化的各个方面是如何共同变化的。(42)______。

lines: In the early 1900s in North America, German-born American anthropologist Franz Boas developed a new theory of culture known as historical particularism. Historical particularism, which emphasized the uniqueness of all cultures, gave new direction to anthropology. (43) ______.
20世纪初在北美，德裔美国人类学家弗朗茨·博厄斯创立了一种新的文化理论，即历史特殊论。历史特殊论强调一切文化的独特性，为人类学指明了新的方向。(43)______。

sentences.en: Historical particularism, which emphasized the uniqueness of all cultures, gave new direction to anthropology.

lines: Boas felt that the culture of any society must be understood as the result of a unique history and not as one of many cultures belonging to a broader evolutionary stage or type of culture. (44) ______.
博厄斯认为，任何社会的文化都必须被理解为一段独特历史的产物，而不能被看作同属于某个更宽泛的进化阶段或文化类型的诸文化之一。(44)______。

lines: Historical particularism became a dominant approach to the study of culture in American anthropology, largely through the influence of many students of Boas. But a number of anthropologists in the early 1900s also rejected the particularist theory of culture in favor of diffusionism. Some attributed virtually every important cultural achievement to the inventions of a few, especially gifted peoples that, according to diffusionists, then spread to other cultures. (45) ______.
主要由于博厄斯众多学生的影响，历史特殊论成为美国人类学中研究文化的主导方法。但20世纪初也有一些人类学家排斥文化特殊论，转而支持传播论。有人几乎把每一项重要的文化成就都归功于少数几个（按传播论者的说法随后传播到其他文化中的）天才民族的发明。(45)______。

lines: There is a marked difference between the education which every one gets from living with others and the deliberate educating of the young. In the former case the education is incidental; it is natural and important, but it is not the express reason of the association. (46) It may be said that the measure of the worth of any social institution is its effect in enlarging and improving experience, but this effect is not a part of its original motive. Religious associations began, for example, in the desire to secure the favor of overruling powers and to ward off evil influences; family life in the desire to gratify appetites and secure family perpetuity; systematic labor, for the most part, because of enslavement to others, etc. (47) Only gradually was the by-product of the institution noted, and only more gradually still was this effect considered as a directive factor in the conduct of the institution. Even today, in our industrial life, apart from certain values of industriousness and thrift, the intellectual and emotional reaction of the forms of human association under which the world's work is carried on receives little attention as compared with physical output.

每个人在与他人共同生活中所受的教育，与对年轻人的刻意教育之间，存在着显著的差别。在前一种情形中，教育是附带发生的；它是自然而重要的，却并不是这种联合的明确目的。(46) 可以说，衡量任何社会制度价值的标准，是其在丰富和改善经验方面的作用，但这种作用并不是其原始动机的一部分。例如，宗教团体的产生，源于希望获得支配性力量的眷顾并躲避邪恶影响；家庭生活的产生，源于满足欲望和确保家族延续的愿望；系统的劳动，在很大程度上则是因为受他人奴役，等等。(47) 人们只是逐渐才注意到制度的这一副产品，而更晚之后，才把这种作用视为制度运作中的指导性因素。即使在今天，在我们的工业生活中，除了勤劳和节俭等某些价值之外，与物质产出相比，承载世间工作的人类各种联合形式在智力和情感上的反应，也几乎无人关注。

sample: I am writing to share my concerns about “white pollution” in our city. Although restrictions on plastic bags were introduced not long ago, free plastic bags are still handed out in many markets, and discarded bags can be seen everywhere along the streets and rivers. Clearly, the policy has yet to take effect.
我写信是想谈谈我对本市“白色污染”的担忧。尽管限塑措施出台不久，但许多市场仍在免费发放塑料袋，街道和河流两旁随处可见被丢弃的塑料袋。显然，这项政策尚未真正见效。

data.image_desc: 图画题目为“网络的'近'与'远'”：一张巨大的蜘蛛网状网络覆盖画面，网的各个格子里是一个个小隔间，每个隔间里坐着一个对着电脑上网的人；人们虽然被网络紧紧连在一起，彼此却隔间相望、近在咫尺又远在天涯。
sample: The drawing presents a huge spider-web-like network that covers the whole picture. In each small compartment of the web sits a person, staring at his own computer. Although they are connected by the same net, they are separated from one another by walls, unable to see or talk to their closest neighbors. The caption reads: the “nearness” and “farness” of the Internet.
这幅图画展示了一张覆盖全图的巨大蜘蛛网状网络。网上的每一个小隔间里都坐着一个人，正盯着自己的电脑。他们虽然被同一张网连接在一起，却又被墙壁彼此隔开，无法看见、也无法与近在咫尺的邻居交谈。图画的标题是：网络的“近”与“远”。

sample: The intended meaning of the picture is thought-provoking: the Internet has indeed shortened the distance between people far apart, yet it may lengthen the distance between those near at hand. On the one hand, we can chat with friends on the other side of the globe at any moment. On the other hand, glued to our screens, we tend to neglect face-to-face communication with family members and neighbors, so that people living next door may feel like strangers.
这幅图的寓意发人深省：网络确实缩短了远隔千里的人们之间的距离，却可能拉长近在身边的人之间的距离。一方面，我们可以随时与地球另一端的朋友聊天。另一方面，当我们紧盯屏幕时，却往往忽视了与家人和邻居面对面的交流，以至于隔壁的邻居形同陌路。

directionSentences.en: In your essay, you should 1) describe the drawing briefly, 2) explain its intended meaning, and then 3) give your comments.
directionSentences.zh: 文章中，你应当：1）简要描述图画；2）解释其寓意；3）发表你的评论。

directionSentences.en: You should write neatly on ANSWER SHEET 2. (20 points)
directionSentences.zh: 请工整地写在答题卡2上。（20分）
